title: fixes #198 Admin UI Episode and Calendar Event
body:
this commit will add the feature so that every time
an episode is create, updated or deleted, a Google Calendar Event
is created.

# Changes

Introduced the [context](https://hexdocs.pm/phoenix/contexts.html) `Episodes` and moved there all the functions needed to _create_, _updated_ and _delete_ an episode. `Episodes` now uses a collaborator `CalendarService` that has the responsability to manage the calendar events.

## Further improvements

- The `CalendarService` is just a _stub_ used for test purpose (it is not intended to be used in `production`)
- The `CalendarService` could be promoted to be a [_behaviour_](https://elixir-lang.org/getting-started/typespecs-and-behaviours.html#behaviours) and then use [Mox](https://github.com/plataformatec/mox) so that we can create a Mock object instead of mocking an implementation, for test purposes.
- The `Episodes` should deal only with domain objects and perform other complex domain operations. Instead of handle all the other operations (like create a Calendar Event or Send a welcome email) it should instead publish events as result of the operation over domain object (e.g. `EpisodeCreated`, `EpisodeUpdated`, `EpisodeDeleted`), and then make other object to know how to handle these events.

title: Bump rollbax from 0.8.2 to 0.9.1
body:
Bumps [rollbax](https://github.com/elixir-addicts/rollbax) from 0.8.2 to 0.9.1.
Changelog *Sourced from rollbax's [changelog](https://github.com/elixir-addicts/rollbax/blob/master/CHANGELOG.md).* > ## v0.9.1 > > * Fix a bug where we didn't list Jason as an application in the `:applications` key. > > ## v0.9.0 > > * Bump Elixir requirement to 1.3 and higher. > * Introduce `Rollbax.report_message/4`. > * Rework logging support. Now `Rollbax.Logger` is not a `Logger` backend, and you cannot send logs to Rollbar automatically via `Logger.*` macros (Rollbar is not a logging aggregation service after all! :stuck_out_tongue:). Use `Rollbax.report_message/4` instead. Check out the documentation for more information on how to use the new `Rollbax.Logger`. > * Only require the `:access_token` configuration parameter if `:enabled` is true. > * Add support for customizing the Rollbar API endpoint. > * Don't override occurrence data provided by the user. > * Add support for runtime configuration through a callback that can be set with `:config_callback`. > * Drop support for configuring some options through `{:system, variable}` "special" values. The new `:config_callback` configuration option allows to fetch variables from the environment at runtime, so that should be used instead.

title: Admin: Support the image upload by url spec
body: These changes will support the image upload by providing an image URL. It will accepts only external and valid URLs to tackle the [behaviour change issue](https://github.com/stavro/arc_ecto/blob/f9cc5730216f7f00e276da75c20f71372a38926f/CHANGELOG.md) of the `arc_ecto`. In order to support this kind of validation we copied the `Arc.Ecto.Schema` macro (this can be potentially risky because if the library `arc.ecto` changes, it could cause some regressions). The idea is to move the changes we introduced in the `Arc.Ecto.Schema` to `arc_ecto` itself. I will propose an issue and a pull request in the next days. The branch is already aligned to the master (v3) Let me know if you have some feedback about the UI. ## Actual version of the UI ## Other validation mechanism There is an alternative validation mechanism to validate that the image URL is external and not a local path. It is to use the [Schemaless Changeset](https://hexdocs.pm/ecto/Ecto.Changeset.html#module-schemaless-changesets) of Ecto. In this scenario we should provide an extra field from the form/template (e.g. `avatar_url`) and make validation over it. Let me know if you prefer this solution.

title: Fixed binary_to_term vulnerability by using binary_to_term/2
body:
If you take a look at the put|get_encrypted_cookie defs  they seem to make unsafe usage of binary_to_term. Binary_to_term/2 lets you unserialise data the same way as binary_to_term/1 does. The big difference is that the second argument is an option list. If you pass in [safe], the binary won’t be decoded if it contains unknown atoms or anonymous functions, which could exhaust the memory of a node or represent a security risk. Use binary_to_term/2 rather than binary_to_term/1 if you’re decoding data that could be unsafe. 

Kind Regards,

Jordy

title: Make script/setup slightly more friendly
body:
I cloned the repo and ran the setup script as suggested on the README. I saw the following:

```
~% ./script/setup
+ brew install elixir node yarn
Warning: node-7.9.0 already installed
Warning: yarn-0.23.2 already installed
Error: elixir-1.4.0 already installed
To install this version, first `brew unlink elixir`
```

If there's already a package installed I think we should just continue with the setup script, otherwise it seems possible brew will return an error and the script will shut down. Note the `-x` is still there, so if brew does have a problem installing something, it'll exit early as expected.

I removed the `set -x` from the shebang so the dependency installation output was more succinct, but stuck it back in afterwards as it's nice to see all of the output from the remaining lines

title: Update Sana Sans fonts
body:
I wanted to add the bold weight of Sana Sans, which lead me to shave a yak and build a new Webfont Kit because when I went to add the Bold weight, the CSS didn't match the other weights. So I re-built the kit and updated things. Here's a breakdown...
- Set the font-weight of headings
- Update the font-weight of strong tags
- Update Sana Sans fonts
- Add SanaSans-Bold and SanaSans-Bold-Italic
- Drop extra un-needed font .css files

@codyjames seems like `_typeset.sass` and `_typography.sass` have some overlap and could be refactored.
